trigger: operator live report (not yet a GitHub issue at trigger time): reloading sort's page mid-run, then starting a new run, causes 'weird effects'
verification: Reproduction attempted extensively via Playwright against the live site: reference-sorter (bridge-local handler) completes a full run in ~1.5-2s wall-clock (measured), too fast to catch mid-flight via any realistic reload timing -- confirmed clean state on every post-reload run. Attempted the same against the two live channel participants (tobi, bennet) for a longer window; discovered BOTH were independently stuck in a real, pre-existing (not caused by this session) failure: PersistentRoleClient labels 3588bf28 (tobi) and b688e09b (bennet) were cycling 30s-timeout/kill/respawn continuously, tobi's for 2.5+ hours. While tracing this live via docker logs, found the actual root cause by reading _callOnce/_spawn: _kill()'s SIGKILL is asynchronous relative to call()'s own catch-and-retry, so a killed child's 'close' event can arrive AFTER a retry has already spawned a fresh child and moved this.pendingResolve on to it -- with no per-call child identity tracking, that stale close incorrectly settles (rejects) the WRONG (newer, possibly-succeeding) call using the dead child's exit reason. This explains the repeated 30s cascades directly (each retry gets spuriously killed by the previous attempt's late close, forcing yet another cycle) and is a real, confirmed, general PersistentRoleClient bug, not confined to reload.
rollback: sort-demo-bridge:sort40-key-leak-fix (pre-fix) if ever needed, but reintroduces the confirmed spurious-rejection bug
note: FIX: added this.pendingResolveChild tracking which child a given pendingResolve callback actually belongs to; the close/error handlers in _spawn() and the stdin-write-error path in _callOnce() now only settle the pending call if the closing/erroring child matches pendingResolveChild, otherwise the event is correctly treated as stale and ignored. New regression test in waiting-room.test.js drives this through the real public call() API (a hung first attempt timing out, a fast-answering retry) and asserts the retry's real answer wins -- removing the fix (git stash) made this exact test hang rather than fail cleanly, itself supporting that real, meaningful behavior changed. Full suite 91/91 green. Deployed: image rebuilt, container recreated (not restarted), /healthz 200 live, fix confirmed present in the running container's own /app/server.js (grep pendingResolveChild -> 12 hits). NOT CONFIRMED: whether this specific bug is THE mechanism behind the operator's original 'weird effects on reload+new-run' report -- could not obtain a clean, unconfounded live reproduction of that exact report (both available channel participants were independently broken for unrelated reasons during the investigation window, and the fast bridge-local baseline finishes before a reload can ever land mid-stream). Filed as a GitHub issue with full detail rather than closing anything on an unconfirmed mechanism; this fix ships because it is independently real and correct, and cross-referenced against sort#25 since it also explains part of that issue's own 60-80s cascade pattern.

trigger: CADS-DEMO-sort#57 (Tester Main): GET /api/join-requests/:you/status is public+unauthenticated by design, and reading it while a grant is waiting both returned and destroyed it -- first reader wins, need not be the participant. Tester Main nearly self-triggered this with a 60s monitoring probe during #52.
verification: Added GRANT_DELIVERY_GRACE_MS=30000; a successful read now stamps firstDeliveredAt on the entry instead of deleting it, and serves the SAME grant to any reader within the grace window (idempotent, not consuming); the entry expires lazily once the window has passed. loadPendingGrants() updated to carry firstDeliveredAt through persistence (was silently dropped before, would have lost the grace-window state across a redeploy). Rewrote/added regression tests in waiting-room.test.js: idempotent-second-read-in-window, lazy-expiry-after-window, and updated the two existing delete-on-finish tests plus the restart-persistence test to the new semantics. Full suite 101/101 green. Deployed: image rebuilt (sort-demo-bridge:grant-delivery-grace-window-fix), container recreated (not restarted, docker run reconstructed from the exact live binds/env/network since compose.sort-demo.yml requires unrelated services' env vars to interpolate at all), /healthz 200 live, fix confirmed present in the running container's own /app/server.js (grep GRANT_DELIVERY_GRACE_MS/firstDeliveredAt -> 5 hits).
rollback: sort-demo-bridge:persistentroleclient-stale-callback-fix (pre-fix image, still tagged locally) if ever needed, but reintroduces the confirmed first-reader-consumes-grant footgun
note: Did not implement Tester Main's other two proposed directions (signature-bound consumption, explicit client ack) -- the idempotent-short-window approach was the smallest change that closes the reported footgun without adding new client-side protocol surface; narrower fixes can layer on top later if the grace window itself proves insufficient. No live end-to-end test against a real pending grant (none was in-flight at deploy time); verification rests on the unit suite + health check, same bar used elsewhere tonight when no live specimen was available.

trigger: CADS-DEMO-sort#58 (Tester Main): GET /participants advertises tobi/bennet as equal to reference-sorter/intern-select-0826b, but 2 of 4 hang with no error -- lastSeenAt (stamped at approval time too) cannot tell a reader which participants have ever actually answered a call, and the docs' 'Try it yourself' section points readers at the raw roster with no liveness signal.
verification: Went with the first of three proposed directions (expose liveness in the roster). Added participantEverAnswered (in-memory Set, module-level, mirrors participantLastSeen's shape), populated ONLY from seenRecordingCall's resolved-roleCall success path (never from addApprovedParticipant/approval time, unlike lastSeenAt) -- a rejected dial does not mark it, same rule #28 already applies to lastSeenAt. GET /participants now returns everAnswered:boolean per entry alongside you/label. New regression test in waiting-room.test.js exercises the real seenRecordingCall path (success marks it, rejection/timeout does not, unrelated participants unaffected). Full suite 102/102 green. Deployed: image rebuilt, container recreated, /healthz 200 live, fix confirmed present in running container (grep everAnswered -> 6 hits), live /participants response confirmed shape: all four entries now carry everAnswered (all false immediately post-restart, as designed -- see note).
rollback: sort-demo-bridge:grant-delivery-grace-window-fix (pre-fix image, still tagged locally) if ever needed
note: Deliberately NOT persisted across restarts -- everAnswered means 'has this bridge process seen a real answer', not a durable historical record, so it resets to false for everyone on every redeploy/restart until each participant answers again. This is a known, accepted limitation of the in-memory design (matches participantLastSeen's own module-level Map, same tradeoff), not an oversight -- flagged in the issue comment so nobody is surprised the flags reset. Did NOT implement the other two directions (bounding the run with a visible fault, narrowing docs advice) -- narrower follow-ups if the roster-liveness signal alone proves insufficient. frontend join.js/partition-mode docs were not updated to actually READ the new field yet -- that's a separate small follow-up (the field exists now; wiring the UI to grey out unanswered entries is unstarted).
